title: Telemetry IaC: Upgrade Guardian for Prometheus/Grafana + OTLP log shipping
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build a robust, opinionated Terraform/Helm module called 'Upgrade Guardian' for the Private (VPC) observability stack. The module should provision Prometheus + Grafana, an OpenTelemetry Collector deployment, and a log-shipping path (Fluent Bit -> S3 or Vector -> S3 depending on customer profile).

Goals:
- Make upgrades safe and reversible: support canary/blue-green upgrade flows, health gating, and automated rollback on health regression.
- Provide standard preflight and postflight health checks that integrate with the deployment pipeline (CI/CD) and with Redwood Console rollouts.
- Reduce blast radius in customer VPCs: enable scoped upgrades per cell/namespace and safe defaults for resource requests, horizontal scaling, and retention.
- Expose a minimal Terraform surface (inputs/outputs) for platform teams and advanced knobs for Dedicated/Private customers.

Design decisions:
- Module structure: top-level Terraform module that manages HelmRelease resources via the Helm provider and a small helper k8s job CRD for migration/cron preflight. Avoid embedding raw chart values in templates; surface config via a limited map variable.
- Upgrade strategy: support 'canary_fraction' and 'grace_period_seconds' variables; module creates a canary namespace and a reconciliation policy that will only promote after N consecutive health checks pass. Health checks include: Prometheus scrape health, Grafana backend health endpoint, collector pipeline lag/throughput, and log shipping S3 ack rate.
- Health checks implementation: lightweight k8s probe jobs that query internal endpoints and emit a Success/Fail CRD. Terraform will create a Kubernetes Job + a simple controller (stateless image) used by the module to evaluate checks. The controller image will be hosted on our internal registry.
- Observability for the observability module: instrument the OTLP collector with an internal metrics pipeline to emit upgrade/health metrics to a side Prometheus scrape target. These metrics will feed into console SLOs and the rollout gating logic.
- Rollback: module wires a guarded hook to the HelmRelease (or to Helm provider lifecycle) that marks the release failed and triggers a rollback if health gating fails. Also produce actionable logs and a runbook link in the failure annotation.
- Config & secrets: support KMS-backed secrets for Grafana admin credentials and TLS certs. Integrate with customer KMS/HSM via secret manager module inputs.

Implementation notes:
- Terraform variables: chart_version, canary_fraction (float), health_window (seconds), required_successes (int), retention_days_prometheus (int), grafana_admin_secret_arn (string), log_shipper_mode (string: fluentbit|vector), s3_bucket_arn (string).
- Outputs: prometheus_endpoint, grafana_endpoint, collector_otlp_endpoint, module_health_endpoint, grafana_admin_secret_arn.
- CI/CD changes: add a pipeline job that runs 'terraform plan' -> deploy to a sandbox cell -> run canary health checks -> promote. The pipeline will call a new API endpoint on the console to mark promotion.

Docs & runbook:
- Confluence: /confluence/display/OBS/Upgrade+Guardian+Module (WIP)
- Runbook: step-by-step rollback, how to re-run checks, and emergency downgrade path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module deploys cleanly into an isolated VPC cell with default settings.
- Canary upgrade path completes and promotes only after required health checks pass.
- Failure path triggers rollback and produces a human-readable failure reason.
- Integration tests that simulate ETL noise and verify that log-shipping a sample batch reaches S3 within acceptable latency.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Health checks are too strict and block legitimate upgrades. Mitigation: expose tuning knobs and include a 'force_promote' flag for SRE-led emergency actions.
- Risk: Helm provider lifecycle conflicts with k8s controllers. Mitigation: rely on explicit job-based checks and avoid custom controllers that mutate HelmRelease state.

Next steps & Implementation plan:
1) Prototype the health job image (1 week) -> internal RFC review.
2) Terraform module skeleton + Helm chart wiring (2 weeks).
3) End-to-end canary flow test in sandbox (1 week).
4) Security review, KMS integration, and Confluence runbook (1 week).

Links: GitHub PR scaffold: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls/6421 (WIP), Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/123456 (internal).
